text: Same agent configuration as operator-loop-20260913, refined by what that campaign learned: every execution worker composes across a same-tier pool (no runtimeDefaults.worker pin) rather than a single pinned runtime -- tonight's three safe candidates were dsh/deepseek-flash, zcode/glm-5.3-flash (permissionMode yolo), agy/gemini-3.8-flash-low, all tier 1, none sharing a vendor with the judge. Judge is always gpt-6-astra via codex, no fallback (a GLM fallback shares vendor with a GLM worker candidate and is refused at execution as judge_fallback_vendor_conflict -- verified live). gpt-5.6-luna is not a worker candidate for the same reason (openai, same vendor as the judge). Astra is also the reviewing architect of the spec; the campaign does not execute until it accepts. Mechanical supervise (--detach) handles controller liveness; no model runs as supervisor.

The campaign must NEVER stop. Every role always has a fallback: workers compose across the tier-1 pool (dsh/deepseek-flash, zcode/glm-flash, agy/gemini-3.8-flash, plus codex/gpt-luna-flash wherever it does not share a vendor with the judge of that node), and when a provider is exhausted the run moves to the next candidate rather than halting. It stops only when every provider in the tier is exhausted at once, and even then it must determine which provider frees its usage first, wait for exactly that instant, and continue on its own -- deterministically, with no operator in the loop. This requirement is the reason phases 1a/1b/1c exist: it is being encoded in the factory's own code, not just in this campaign's operating procedure.

Routing for this campaign, superseding the earlier note that pinned gpt-6-astra as judge: the judge is claude-opus-5 via the claude harness (vendor anthropic, permissionMode plan, tier 2). Anthropic is not a worker vendor, so the worker pool is the full set originally asked for -- dsh/deepseek-flash, zcode/glm-5.3-flash, agy/gemini-3.8-flash-low, codex/gpt-5.6-luna -- all tier 1, all different vendors, none colliding with the judge. runtimeDefaults declares judge only; the worker is left composed so it walks the whole tier on exhaustion instead of taking a single fallback hop. Reason for the change: gpt-6-astra exhausted its usage mid-campaign twice, and a judge that blocks every gate is the worst place to have a single point of failure.

Spec accepted at v6 after six review rounds (rounds 1-2 REJECT, 3-4 ACCEPT WITH CHANGES under gpt-6-astra, 5 ACCEPT WITH CHANGES and 6 ACCEPT under the glm-5.3 fallback judge). Accepted text committed at skills/mine/intent-factory/docs/campaigns/operator-loop-followup-20260914/spec/SPEC-accepted.md (commit ba74eff). Two defects were found and fixed during the dialogue that no amount of static reading would have caught: storing exhaustion evidence inside state.error, which every dispatch wipes; and clearing the generation counter together with the evidence, which reset the generation to its implicit 0 and resurrected a stale exclusion set. Both are why the final design keeps routing.tierExhaustionCycle outside routing.tierExhaustion.

Phase 1 launched as run followup-phase1-20260914 (contract followup-phase1-20260914, 3 nodes: tier-exhaustion-evidence -> tier-exhaustion-retry -> tier-exhaustion-supervision), controller pid 1951 detached, supervisor --detach started. Two environment facts the next operator must know: (1) the launch runs under an interactive zsh because DEEPSEEK_API_KEY and ZAI_API_KEY are exported only in ~/.zshrc and this harness's bash environment does not inherit them -- a plain bash launch leaves dsh-deepseek-flash and zcode-glm-flash unavailable with authentication_required, silently shrinking the worker pool to agy-gemini-flash and codex-luna-flash; (2) the provider CLIs persist state under $HOME (~/.claude, ~/.codex, ~/.dsh, ~/.zcode, CODEX_HOME) so the controller must run with unrestricted file access, not a workspace-only sandbox. Phases 2 and 3 are independent of phase 1 and of each other per the accepted spec's Delivery section, but all three integrate into the same repository, so they will be launched sequentially as each predecessor reaches terminal, never concurrently.

Operator incident, self-inflicted and recovered: the first controller (pid 1951, launched under interactive zsh) was stopped to attach the Ford notify transport, but its replacement resume --detach was launched from a plain bash shell that had only the Ford env sourced and NOT DEEPSEEK_API_KEY -- so attempt 2 died immediately with MISSING_CREDENTIAL on dsh-deepseek-flash, the node went failed and its two dependents blocked, and the run parked in attention with needsYou 3. Two lessons for the next operator: (1) sourcing ~/.config/intent-factory-notify-ford/env is not a substitute for the worker credentials, which live only in ~/.zshrc -- every launch, resume and supervise must run under interactive zsh AND source the Ford env, because the mechanical supervisor re-launches resume with its own inherited environment, so a supervisor started without the worker keys silently poisons every future resume; (2) recovery is cheap by design: attempt 1 had been sealed at 8611938 before the interruption, attempt 2 was cut from that sealed sha, and resume after the fix dispatched attempt 3 from the same base, so no sealed work was lost. The run is back to active 0/3, node tier-exhaustion-evidence running at attempt 3, needsYou 0, controller pid 11561, supervisor pid 13290, and notify.jsonl now records delivered receipts -- the Ford transport is confirmed live. Phone access to this harness was also set up: tailscale serve is unusable on this tailnet because it cannot obtain TLS certs, so a minimal TCP bridge (node, /tmp/dsh-web-bridge.mjs) binds the tailnet address 100.126.74.93:3080 and forwards to the loopback-only DSH web server; the GUI still requires the launch token, which is minted in memory per dsh web process and is therefore never recoverable from disk.

Standing campaign policy, superseding any operator-in-the-loop reading of the workflow: the campaign must never idle between phases, and an integration-policy question is never a reason to stop. Phase 1 reached terminal (3/3 done, all pass, $3.38) and the run sat finished for ~2h while the orchestrator waited for a human answer on whether to advance main or accumulate on a branch; that stall is the defect this note closes, not the run, which never stalled. The policy the orchestrator must now apply without asking: accumulate on the work branch (work/operator-loop-followup-20260914) and never move main; promotion to main is the owner's reversible call (git checkout main && git merge --ff-only work/operator-loop-followup-20260914). The structural gap is in the factory, not in this campaign's procedure: supervise keeps ONE run finishing but nothing chains one contract to the next, so a phase boundary is where autonomy ends. That gap is closed for this campaign by .runs/campaigns/operator-loop-followup-20260914/chain.sh, a detached mechanical driver that owns no run state and takes no lock -- it launches a phase with run --detach, blocks on the existing deterministic supervise until every node is terminal, refuses to promote a run whose status is not done, merges the run ref into the work branch with --ff-only, and proceeds to the next phase. No model runs in that loop. Any future orchestrator must treat a terminal phase as an instruction to launch the next one, never as a question for the operator.

chain.sh attempt 1 failed and attempt 2 succeeded; both defects were in the driver, not in the factory. Defect one: the promote gate read .state from the RUN's own status.json, which has no such field -- its top level is campaignId, contractId, controller, goal, identityWarnings, nodes, run, schemaVersion, summary, usage, and the .state that exists belongs to the .runs/status.json pointer, which tracks whichever run is newest. So a phase-2 run that had genuinely finished (next-rank-absence done attempt 1, verdict pass, 1m37s) was read as null and refused promotion. The gate now reads the run's own nodes and requires at least one: (.nodes|length)>0 and all(.nodes[]; .status=="done" or .status=="no-op"), so an empty snapshot can never pass vacuously. Defect two: the driver was launched inside a shell pipeline ending in grep, so the script's exit 1 was masked by grep's exit 0 and the launch reported success while the chain had already stopped. The relaunch redirects stderr to a file instead of piping. Attempt 2 then ran phase 2 idempotently -- run directory already present, so it supervised the finished run rather than starting over -- fast-forwarded d32a52c..4e16e5c into work/operator-loop-followup-20260914 (report/next.mjs +17, test/report/next.test.mjs +43) and launched phase 3 from 4e16e5c. Residual risk worth naming: when the driver exits 1 on a genuine block nothing restarts it, so the chain layer is still unsupervised even though each run is. Closing that needs a LaunchAgent or an in-repo chain capability.

Delivered to main at c161a95 (5/5 nodes done across 3 runs, 4.37h wall clock, $4.38, silentStallRate 0, blocking-judge first-pass rate 1.0 -- not one gate rejection in the whole campaign). Full suite 746 pass / 1 fail, where the single failure is test/harnesses/dsh.test.mjs's live 'a real harness turns one prompt into a result with real tokens' returning failed after 904s because DeepSeek was down; the campaign touched neither test/harnesses/ nor src/harnesses/, so that test and its subject are byte-identical on both branches, and re-running the directory with DEEPSEEK_API_KEY unset gives 128 pass / 0 fail / 1 skipped. Typecheck clean; deterministic evals 17/17 passing and 17/17 discriminating. WHAT TO REPEAT. The composed four-vendor worker pool did its job: no node was ever blocked by provider exhaustion, which is exactly the failure that cost the previous campaign hours. claude-opus-5 as judge passed every gate on the first blocking review and still arbitrated substantively -- it caught that phase 3 needed src/run/usage.mjs (one typedef line) outside its writeFiles and allowed precisely that, rather than rubber-stamping or failing the node. Above all, the six-round spec dialogue paid for itself: it caught two design defects that no amount of static reading would have found -- storing exhaustion evidence inside state.error, which every dispatch wipes, and clearing the generation counter together with the evidence, which resets the generation to its implicit 0 and resurrects a stale exclusion set. Both were found by a judge executing the code, not reading it. IMPROVEMENT 1 -- credentials are invisible to preflight. The first node burned two attempts (one cancel, one MISSING_CREDENTIAL) because DEEPSEEK_API_KEY and ZAI_API_KEY are exported only in ~/.zshrc and a bash launch does not inherit them. preflight and 'models --probe' both reported every runtime reachable, because they probe the binary and never the credential the binary needs.
